Thanks for the time on Tuesday. Attached is our draft mutual action plan (PharmaCare_MAP_v1.pdf) and the detailed performance validation workbook (pharmacare_perf_plan.xlsx). The plan focuses on the three checkpoints you asked for during the POC:

- Latency (p95 / median) for 1–2 concurrent requests and at target concurrency (50 RPS)
- Throughput and TTFT (time-to-first-token) for bursty traffic and sustained loads
- Quality vs. cost for three Redwood catalog variants we discussed (Rwd-XL, Rwd-Lite-Quant, Rwd-Base-8bit)

High-level ask: please confirm the KPI targets in the MAP column marked in yellow by EOD Friday (7/3). If you agree, we’ll run the baseline tests next week and deliver a short summary plus artifact (CSV+plots) you can upload to your evaluation workbook.

Quick notes:
- We’ll run warm-cache and cold-cache scenarios and report both (prefixed in CSV).
- For throughput tests we’ll use our continuous-batching path to reflect realistic real-time routing.
- We recommend starting with Rwd-Lite-Quant for latency-sensitive UI flows and Rwd-Base-8bit for low-cost background generation. The evaluation plan has the acceptance criteria per use case.

Olivia / team —

Following up with the initial baseline run we completed against the MAP target profile (stages: 10/25/40/50 RPS). Summary below; full CSV attached (benchmark_results_v1.csv) and plots in Drive link.

Baseline (warm-cache) results, 8k token sequences typical of PharmaCare long-form summarization tests:
- Rwd-XL: p95 latency = 320ms, median = 120ms, sustained throughput at 50 RPS (95th percentile CPU/GPU util stable)
- Rwd-Lite-Quant: p95 latency = 210ms, median = 95ms, best TTFT at single-request flows
- Rwd-Base-8bit: p95 latency = 480ms, median = 210ms, best cost/token at scale (20–30% cheaper)

Concurrency degradation: Rwd-Lite-Quant shows graceful degradation between 40->50 RPS (p95 increases ~35ms). Rwd-XL holds latency under 350ms p95 up to 50 RPS but at ~2.2x the per-token cost vs Rwd-Lite-Quant. Rwd-Base-8bit remains the cheapest for background batch jobs but fails the 250ms p95 SLO for interactive UI.

Quality checks (seeded with PharmaCare top-20 prompts + Redwood evals): initial human scoring (n=200 samples per variant) shows: 
- Rwd-XL: highest quality (semantic accuracy ~92%)
- Rwd-Lite-Quant: ~88% accuracy, occasional verbosity in long context
- Rwd-Base-8bit: ~82% accuracy, more hallucination in rare entities

Conclusion / recommendation: For interactive clinician UI flows where p95 < 300ms matters, pilot Rwd-Lite-Quant with aggressive prefix caching + 2x warm instances. For scheduled batch summaries (overnight), use Rwd-Base-8bit to optimize cost. See attached CSV for per-run metrics and cold-cache CSV sheet.

Attachments: benchmark_results_v1.csv

Olivia —

Thanks for the questions and great feedback. A few concrete next items (I copied the Drive/HubSpot links into the MAP):

- Staged concurrency: we ran 10 / 25 / 40 / 50 RPS. Full degradation table is in the CSV and the latency_plots.png.
- Dedicated test hardware: the run used NVidia H100, 80GB, with our continuous batch allocator (this maps to the Dedicated Sku we quoted). If PharmaCare wants a different config (A100 series) we can re-run but expect ~10–20% lower throughput.
- Quality evaluation: we used your top-20 prompts for human scoring and paired them with the Redwood public eval set to compute delta scores. Those artifacts are available in Drive (link below).

Suggested plan:
1) Sign the light SOW and reserve an H100 pool for two weeks (explicit window: 7/20–8/3) — this lets us run the extended stress runs and runway tests.
2) Pilot Rwd-Lite-Quant on the clinician UI traffic for 2 weeks with live tracing; if p95 stays <300ms and quality delta <4% vs Rwd-XL, open a staged rollout to 20% traffic.
3) For batch summarization, configure Rwd-Base-8bit with 2x batching to maximize cost savings and re-evaluate quality drift after 3 days.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HC-9921), Drive artifacts (https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid/perf-evidence)

If procurement confirms the SOW, we’ll schedule the reserved pool and I’ll own the test-run orchestration.
